findings.current: “Of course. You’ve praised Young Master Wongong so often I’ve got calluses on my ears.”
findings.defect: Mujin says 주인공, meaning “protagonist,” not Wongong. This is the mistake that sets up Ju Wongong’s correction.
findings.rationale: Mujin has mistaken Ju Wongong’s name for the ordinary Korean word 주인공.
findings.replacement: “Of course. You’ve praised Young Master Protagonist so often I’ve got calluses on my ears.”
findings.source: “그럼요. 평소에도 주인공 공자님에 관련된 칭찬을 귀에 못이 박이도록 하지 않으셨습니까.”

findings.current: “See? You heard him, Young Master Wongong.”
findings.defect: Jin repeats Mujin’s mistaken name, but the draft gives him the correct one.
findings.rationale: Both men make the same mistake before Ju Wongong corrects them.
findings.replacement: “See? You heard him, Young Master Protagonist.”

findings.defect: The correction no longer identifies what they called him.
findings.rationale: Ju Wongong explicitly contrasts 주인공 with his name, 주원공.

findings.current: All the while keeping a close eye on Ju Hwaran, who had her hand clamped over his mouth.
findings.defect: The draft makes Hwaran cover someone else’s mouth; she is covering her own.
findings.rationale: The Korean describes Ju Hwaran covering her mouth, without introducing another person as the object of the action.
findings.replacement: All the while keeping a close eye on Ju Hwaran, who had her hand clamped over her mouth.
findings.source: 어느새 입을 틀어막고 있는 주화란을 예의주시하면서.

findings.current: “His Highness, Young Master Ju Wongong, is passing!”
findings.defect: “His Highness” grants Ju Wongong a form of address the herald does not use.
findings.rationale: The announcement calls him 주원공 공자, not 전하.
findings.replacement: “Make way for Young Master Ju Wongong!”

findings.current: “You were about to collapse after running a few dozen yards just now.”
findings.defect: Thirty-odd jang is roughly a hundred yards, not a few dozen yards.
findings.rationale: The draft substantially shortens the distance Jin says Ju Wongong ran.
findings.replacement: “You were about to collapse after running barely a hundred yards just now.”
findings.source: “아까 겨우 삼십여 장 달리고 쓰러지려고 하던데.”

findings.current: “Of course you don’t! Your eyes were already rolling back in your head!”
findings.defect: Rolling eyes suggest fainting; Ju Wongong is referring to Jin having lost control in anger.
findings.rationale: Jin’s claim not to remember follows his furious beating of Mujin, not a loss of consciousness.
findings.replacement: “Of course you don’t! You’d already gone wild by then!”

findings.current: “Listen, everyone! Young Master Wongong, a member of the imperial family, has insulted His Highness Prince Shangshan!”
findings.defect: Jin deliberately uses the wrong name again, while the draft calls Ju Wongong by a near-correct name.
findings.rationale: The renewed 주인공 mistake prompts Ju Wongong’s immediate correction.
findings.replacement: “Listen, everyone! Protagonist, a member of the imperial family, has insulted His Highness Prince Shangshan!”
findings.source: “모두 들어라! 황족 주인공이 상산왕 전하를 모욕했다!”

findings.current: “I’m not Wongong, I’m Ju Wongong! And would you please stop!”
findings.defect: Ju Wongong corrects “protagonist,” not the shortened form “Wongong.”
findings.rationale: His repeated correction is the payoff to Jin’s deliberate misnaming.
findings.replacement: “It’s Ju Wongong, not Protagonist! And would you please stop!”

findings.current: I repented of my old ways, when I did nothing but indulge in wine and women…
findings.defect: The draft omits gambling and other idle amusements from what Ju Wongong claims to have repented.
findings.rationale: 주색잡기 encompasses drinking, women, gambling, and frivolous pursuits.
findings.replacement: I repented of my old ways, when I did nothing but drink, chase women, and gamble…

findings.current: his only real talent was indulging in wine and women.
findings.defect: The later characterization again drops gambling from Ju Wongong’s vices.
findings.replacement: his only real talent was drinking, chasing women, and gambling.

findings.current: I was changing his diapers and everything.
findings.defect: The draft softens Jin’s deliberately crude diaper claim.
findings.rationale: Jin explicitly says 똥 기저귀, which helps make the claim more embarrassing.
findings.replacement: I was even changing his poopy diapers.
findings.source: 내가 똥 기저귀도 갈아 주고 그랬는데.

summary: The draft preserves the scene’s broad sequence, but it loses the name joke, changes one physical action, inflates Ju Wongong’s title, and alters several concrete details.
